# Evaluation: taxonomy and blueprint generator

The numbers below are generated by `cargo run -p xtask -- eval --write`, which downloads each
dataset at a pinned revision and sha256 into the gitignored `.cache/eval/`, runs the shipped
gazetteer and title normalizer over it, and splices the result into this file. `eval --check`
reproduces them and fails if they drift.

<!-- eval:begin (generated by `cargo run -p xtask -- eval --write`; do not edit) -->
### SkillSpan test split: gazetteer spans vs. skill + knowledge annotations

| subset | gold spans | predicted | precision (exact) | recall (exact) | precision (overlap) | recall (overlap) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| house | 1019 | 159 | 40.3% | 6.3% | 57.2% | 8.8% |
| tech | 1245 | 407 | 58.7% | 19.2% | 74.4% | 23.8% |
| all | 2264 | 566 | 53.5% | 13.4% | 69.6% | 17.0% |

### TechWolf synthetic ESCO skill sentences: is the target skill found?

| sentences | target resolvable | recall (same concept) | recall (same, broader or narrower) | predictions | precision (lower bound) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 138260 | 137200 | 19.2% | 19.3% | 40129 | 65.6% |

### TalentCLEF 2025 Task A, English validation: job-title normalization

| queries | resolved to an occupation | MAP (taxonomy) | MAP (folded-string baseline) | MAP (ESCO only; leaks gold labels) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 105 | 88.6% | 0.040 | 0.012 | 0.031 |

## Reading the numbers

These are modest numbers. They measure a dictionary matcher, not a learned model, and each
dataset's annotation differs from what the gazetteer is built to find.

**SkillSpan.** Annotators marked skill and knowledge spans, and many of those are verb phrases
("work independently", "communicate with stakeholders"). The gazetteer finds taxonomy concept
names, and the postings scope it runs in here (see below) deliberately skips soft skills.
Exact-span recall is 13.4% overall: 19.2% on the tech postings and 6.3% on the house postings,
whose annotations are mostly soft skills. Overlap recall is 17.0%. Overlap precision is 69.6%:
about seven in ten things the gazetteer reports are something an annotator also marked. The rest
includes skills the annotators did not mark and taxonomy names used as ordinary words. The
case-sensitivity rules, the stoplist and the postings scope in `curated.yaml` exist to cut the
second kind.

**TechWolf.** Each sentence was generated by a language model to express one ESCO skill. The
taxonomy embeds ESCO's labels, which should favour the gazetteer. It still finds the target in
only 19.2% of sentences (19.3% counting one broader or narrower hop), because the sentences
paraphrase the skill instead of naming it, and because many targets are ESCO alternative labels,
one-word labels or transversal skills, which the postings scope does not report. The sentences target ESCO v1.1.0. In 1,060 of them,
the target label does not resolve in v1.2.1, so they are left out of recall. Precision is a lower bound: each sentence has one gold
skill, so a correct mention of a second skill counts as wrong.

**TalentCLEF Task A.** The task ranks about 2,600 corpus titles for each query. The normalizer
does not rank. It maps the query to an occupation and puts every corpus title that maps to the
same occupation first, in corpus order. Even when 88.6% of queries resolve, MAP is 0.040. This is
above the folded-string baseline (0.012) but far below the systems submitted to the task.
Restricting resolution to ESCO, the taxonomy the gold groups come from, scores lower (0.031), not
higher. Embedding ESCO's labels therefore does not turn this into a lookup: the groups the qrels
use are finer than ESCO occupation concepts, and many corpus titles resolve to a neighbouring
concept or to none.

## The postings scope: before and after

A blueprint generator turns every mention into a requirement, so its gazetteer
(`Scope::Postings`) indexes less of ESCO than the one a scorer uses on resumes
(`Scope::Resumes`, which is only matched against skills a blueprint already names). For
ESCO-source concepts it keeps multi-word preferred labels, curated aliases and the curated
`gazetteer_esco_allow` list ("DevOps", "GDPR", "PostgreSQL"), and drops alternative labels
("email" for electronic communication, "radar" for one of several radar skills), one-word labels
("plan", "logging", "migration") and labels opening with a transversal or attitude verb in
`gazetteer_posting_excluded_prefixes` ("show commitment", "demonstrate curiosity"). "Analyze"
joined the stoplist. Scoring real postings had turned all of these into required skills.

| measure | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| SkillSpan overlap precision (all) | 53.4% | 69.6% |
| SkillSpan overlap recall (all) | 27.7% | 17.0% |
| SkillSpan overlap recall (tech) | 32.6% | 23.8% |
| SkillSpan spans predicted | 1200 | 566 |
| TechWolf recall (same, broader or narrower) | 31.5% | 19.3% |
| TechWolf precision (lower bound) | 42.1% | 65.6% |
| TechWolf predictions | 95823 | 40129 |
| TalentCLEF MAP | 0.040 | 0.040 |

Recall falls because both datasets annotate soft skills and paraphrased ESCO labels, which the
postings scope skips by design; precision rises by 16 and 24 points. Keeping multi-word
alternative labels instead would have recovered about two points of SkillSpan recall and seven
of TechWolf recall at four to six points of precision; it was left out because alternative labels
are where the real-posting noise came from. TalentCLEF measures titles and is unaffected.

## What the regression tests hold

`xtask/src/eval/tests.rs` re-scores the committed samples offline: every 10th SkillSpan
sentence, every 100th TechWolf row, and the full English validation split of Task A. It fails if
a score drops below a floor set just under the value measured when the samples were committed.
The floors guard against regressions. They are not quality targets. When the postings scope landed, the
recall floors were lowered and the precision floors raised to sit under the new measurements; the
reason is recorded beside them.

## Not measured

- **Blueprint generation end to end.** No public dataset pairs job descriptions with
  required-versus-preferred skill labels under a license we can use. The generator's section
  logic is covered by unit tests and by the ArtCraft posting
  (`tests/fixtures/jd/artcraft-hn-2026-11-02.txt`), whose generated required set matches the
  stack the posting lists.
- **Occupation inference from skills.** There is no labelled set to measure it on; the unit
  tests hold two cases. Raw overlap picked O*NET Blockchain Engineers (15-1299.07) for Rust,
  TypeScript, React and PostgreSQL under a vague title ("Senior Engineer"). The cause is not a
  long list that happens to contain the stack: Blockchain Engineers lists 50 technologies and
  names all four, while O*NET 31.0 lists Rust for only two occupations, and not for Software
  Developers (430 technologies, three of the four). Dividing overlap by list length
  (`shared / sqrt(len)` or Jaccard) therefore makes the choice worse, since it favours short
  lists. Inference now scores `shared × ln(len)`, treating a long list as O*NET's record of an
  occupation seen across many postings, and picks Software Developers (15-1252.00) here. Every
  generated blueprint stays `reviewed: false` because this is a prior, not a measurement.
